3266f050d55e3a61.h:
Cult-related homicide

Matamoros, Tamaulipas, Mexico

April 1989

Kidnapping and ritual killing of Mark Kilroy, a University of Texas student, and several Mexican citizens, "sacrificed by orders of drug dealer and Mayombero, Adolfo de Jesus Costanzos" (the primer's spelling). The primer reports that scholars of Afro-Caribbean belief systems call the case an aberration in which Costanzo used Palo Mayombe to convince his drug-trade workers they would be protected, while others hold that Kilroy was a human sacrifice his belief required.

Gayle Olson-Raymer, Occult Crime: A Law Enforcement Primer, California Office of Criminal Justice Planning, 1989 (NCJ 124094), pages 30 and 32. Placed at Matamoros, the town the primer names (the bodies were found at Rancho Santa Elena outside it).

2982bfe04c74eedc.h:
Cult-related homicide

Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, United States

8 September 1985 and 1986

Sean Sellers, who as a 14-year-old began "dabbling in Satanic theology and ritual", shot and killed convenience store clerk Robert Bower with a friend, and months later shot and killed his mother and stepfather. His defense unsuccessfully argued that being under the control of Satan constitutes insanity.

Gayle Olson-Raymer, Occult Crime: A Law Enforcement Primer, California Office of Criminal Justice Planning, 1989 (NCJ 124094), page 32. The primer names no town; Oklahoma City is from Wikipedia's article on Sean Sellers (the killings of his mother and stepfather were in their Oklahoma City home).

4c82ea08610497e8.h:
Cult-related homicide

Carl Junction, Missouri, United States

6 December 1987

Three teenagers, Jim Hardy, Pete Roland and Ron Clements, bludgeoned Steve Newberry to death, according to later court testimony offering "a sacrifice to Satan." At Roland's trial the accused testified "I did as I was told." The defense's insanity plea failed.

Gayle Olson-Raymer, Occult Crime: A Law Enforcement Primer, California Office of Criminal Justice Planning, 1989 (NCJ 124094), page 32. Placed at Carl Junction, the town the primer names.

2853a68d0c817d6a.h:
Cult-related homicide

South of Market, San Francisco, California, United States

15 June 1985 (found); verdict 17 March 1988

The body of a 25-year-old man (John Doe #60) was found with very little blood, patterned injuries, a pentagram carved on the chest and wax in one eye; the San Francisco Police Department linked it to a Satanic ritual. Clifford St. Joseph was convicted of first-degree murder, sodomy and false imprisonment, and sentenced on 5 May 1988 to 34 years to life. The primer gives it as Legal Casestudy #4, a successfully prosecuted case.

Gayle Olson-Raymer, Occult Crime: A Law Enforcement Primer, California Office of Criminal Justice Planning, 1989 (NCJ 124094), pages 53 to 54. Placed in the South of Market area the primer names.

Gang map · Gangs of Los Angeles (2026)

E/S Blacc Menace Mafia Crips

Section: Antelope Valley, Santa Clarita Valley, & Ventura County

Based in the Windrose Apartments, BMM/BMMC was originally started as a Black rag clique founded by BPS members in 1995 at Antelope Valley High School simply known as Black Menace Mafia. The original clique mainly composed of Bloods, Crips, and non-affiliates and was meant to protect Black teens in the neighborhood from racist white skinhead groups in Lancaster before becoming a gang by the early 2000s after beefs with local gangs arose. For the past two decades BMMC has mainly been involved in beefs with local GC sets from the Antelope Valley area, with BIGC being their main rivals. For this reason is why the current younger generation has since turned Mafia Crip. As with most, if not all independent cliques are eventually forced to turn Blood or Crip due to county jail and prison yard gang politics. They also beef with PINMB, FMGC, MHGC, TBHC (sometimes), L13, DSM13, MWC13, and most other Gangster Crip gangs.

W/S Val Verde Park 13 🇲🇽 (Santa Clarita) 

Section: Antelope Valley, Santa Clarita Valley, & Ventura County

One of the oldest and most notorious latino street gangs in the 661 Santa Clarita Valley and Antelope Valley area. Val Verde Park originated in the 1960s as the area of Val Verde was a segregated community where many African Americas found sanctuary in the area and resided there but by the 1950s many Mexican-American workers resided in the community which led to tension between the segregated sides and by the 1960s Val Verde Park was formed as a club/protection for many Mexican-American workers and youth. This is the original barrio of VVP which is known as the Smoke Town Click due to the high amount of crime throughout the years although most of VVP activities can be found in the Antelope Valley (Palmdale). Historically Barrio Val Verde Park 13 main rival has been Barrio Newhall 13 but they also feud with other SCV gangs such as BF13 and other Canyon Country based gangs.

E/S Brown Familia 13 🇲🇽

Section: Antelope Valley, Santa Clarita Valley, & Ventura County

Most hated hood in the Santa Clarita Valley Brown Familia 13 are a Latino street gang based in the Park Sierra Projects on Jakes Way though you can also find them throughout all of Jakes Way. The Brown Familia 13 originated in the early 1990s as a click/crew known as Young But Famous but towards the mid to late 1990s the YBF crew transitioned into a Hispanic/Latino gang known as Brown Familia 13 they are the only dominant and reputable gang in the Canyon Country area of the SCV. Clicks are 23rd Ave, Evil Locos, Hillside Locos and the Midget Locos who also formed a click in Lancaster. Brown Familia 13 historically has a heavy rivalry with the Barrio Newhall 13 which makes up for most of the gang crimes in the Santa Clarita Valley other rivals are BVVP13, CNS13 (WSL13), SSR13, MMS13, WC, R60sNHC, R90sNHC, P13K, PCKF13 and other Antelope Valley Sureno, Blood, Crip and White Supremacist gangs

Old and largest latino street gang in the Santa Clarita Valley, Newhall 13 originated in the 1970s as many migrate workers from Mexico worked in the onion fields and resided on the Eastside of Newhall specifically on 13th Street and Walnut Street many of the youths would hang out together in the neighborhood. Barrio Newhall has many clicks scattered throughout Eastside Newhall with 120 members in total theses clicks include Walnut Locos, Alley Cats, Tiny Locos, Krazy Winos, Eight Ball Boys-(was its own hood before getting into Newhall), Arch Street Locos, Youngsters and Rascals. Barrio Newhall 13 rivals are Brown Familia 13 who they feud with heavily and is responsible for most of the gang related crime in the Santa Clarita Valley other rivals include BVVP13, R60sNHC, CNS13, WSL13, SSR13, MMS13, WC, PBS13, VSF13, P13K, PCK13, BPS13 and various Pacoima sets.

Based in the Pierce Park Apartments, are also known as Nam Gang. Their main clique is 12600/12700 Namstarz, though they have several cliques spread throughout east side Pacoima and Lake View Terrace. Section: San Fernando Valley

Main cliques are 8600 and 9200 Block, LSGB are a Blood gang located in Panorama City that mostly beef with DEGC and WAGC. Founded in 1984, this is one of the most active and deeper Black gangs in the Valley currently. LSGB gained further notoriety due to a surge of activeness in the late 2010s, as LSGB youths consistently went viral on social media for beating up random rivals from DEGC, 87GC, ECC, XV3, CPA13, and whoever else during random incidents across the San Fernando Valley. Though due to the demographics of Panorama City being mostly Hispanic many of their younger members are actually based out of Lancaster/Palmdale despite being a LA/SFV gang. Many of their older members are either incarcerated or have relocated as well. They also beef with 1ECC, OVGC, CST13, CPA13, VCT13, and XV3.  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fyc0Xx7CqRI

E/S Whitsett Avenue Gangster Crips

Section: San Fernando Valley

Part of 3-Pacc, main cliques are 5900 and 6500. 7100 is still claimed to a lesser extent (567), as due to local racial demographics most gang activity north of Vanowen Street is from ALS13 and MS13. WAGC are a GC/3X set based in the North Hollywood district that was formed at Grant High School in 1988 as a black rag gang. Big Paybacc and his early virality on a street level was considered pivotal to his "Gangstaz Got Next" movement in the early 2010s, a slogan that highlighted the GC's efforts to gain a buzz the LA rap industry which was previously dominated by Neighborhood Crip (NHC) and Blood rappers, two of the Gangster Crip/3X card's primary historical rivals.

Upper-middle class and predominately White city on the eastern ridge of the San Fernando Valley. Unlike bordering neighborhoods North Hollywood and Sun Valley; Burbank is not part of the city of Los Angeles as is its own town. On the flipside, Burbank (similar to Glendale and other nearby cities) is also a former sundown town and to this day still has a reputation via BPD for discriminating and profiling Armenian, Middle Eastern, Hispanic, and African Americans in the city, even those that clearly have no ties to any gang activities. BPD also made headlines after being caught dropping off members of their homeless population in neighboring North Hollywood (which is part of LA). Due to their reputation, BPD itself is heavily disliked by both non-affiliate civilians and gang members locally, and VBS13 in particular gained notoriety after killing a BPD officer in a shootout back in 2003.

W/S Armenian Power 13 🇦🇲 (Glendale)

Section: San Fernando Valley

Glendale Gangsters clique (GGS), this is one of AP13's larger hoods based in Glendale (and Burbank to a lesser extent). The Grandview/Glenwood sections of Glendale has historically had one of the largest Armenian-American communities both in California and the entire country. Despite nowadays mainly operating on a "mafia" type scale and being heavily involved in white collar crimes, Armenian Power 13 has remained the most notorious gang in the city and has been responsible for many high-profile gang-related murder, extortion, and fraud cases. This has led to several federal indictments from the FBI in what's otherwise considered one of the safest and most expensive cities in Los Angeles County. Their notoriety has resulted in very few Latino gangs even attempting to "set up shop" in the city (Toonerville Rifa 13 and West Side Locos 13 being the only ones, though TVR13's existence predates the growth of the Armenian community and emergence of AP13 in the city by nearly fifty years). Their beef with TVR13 is also heightened by the fact that TVR13 heavily recruits youths from the Armenian-American community, which is AP13's sole demographic (other Eastern European and Middle Eastern youths being the rare exception). AP13 has also gained media attention for internal conflicts, as infighting amongst members has resulted in several deadly broad day shootings outside Armenian-owned businesses across the Valley. They primarily beef with TVR13, WSLS13, WF13, and MS13.

Small predominately Black and White unincorporated enclave town north of it's twin city Pasadena. Unlike Pasadena, Altadena has never been known for much gang activity outside of the Altadena Blocc Crips (ABC). PDLB did attempt to setup shop here in the form of the Altadena Denver Lane Bloods (ADLB) multiple times throughout the 1980s onwards, but were pretty much given the boot by ABC and pushed back south into Pasadena. Unfortunately, most of their hood and half of the city itself burnt to a crisp during the January 2025 wildfires that spread throughout SoCal.

W/S Pasadena Denver Lane Bloods

Section: San Gabriel Valley & Inland Empire

Large Blood gang in Pasadena, main cliques are Summit Street (559), Tip Top Bloods (882), Project Gangster Bloods (754), Snake Pitt, and Flame Boys. PDLB are a long-established Blood gang in Pasadena whose roots trace back to being stamped by the original LA Denver Lane Bloods during the 1980s. They have remained closely tied to the LA set ever since. PDLB are widely regarded as one of the largest and most active Blood gangs in the San Gabriel Valley, to the point that some of their internal cliques or sub-sets have grown to operate almost like independent gangs of their own, such as SLB and ADLB. Because of their size, activity, and reputation, PDLB have long been one of the most hated gangs in the San Gabriel Valley, resulting in a wide range of rivalries that extend beyond Pasadena into Los Angeles and even parts of San Bernardino County. They mainly beef with ABC, BGC, DRGC, VBP13, and most other Gangster Crip gangs.

W/S Du Roc Gangster Crips (Monrovia)

Section: San Gabriel Valley & Inland Empire

Main cliques are High End and Low End, DRGC is reputable SGV-based Gangster Crip/3X set based in both Monrovia and Duarte to a lesser extent, which is where the name originates from. DRGC historically mainly beefs with PDLB from Pasadena, though also has longstanding locals beefs with DES13, EMF13, and MNV13. DRGC's beef with PDLB is most known, as DRGC members have long been known to take trips back-and-forth to Pasadena down the 210 Freeway to shoot PDLB members (and vice versa). DRGC's murders of EMF13 members is the main reason EMF13 started targeting random Black civilians in the city of El Monte; regardless of gang affiliation. Ironically, despite the numerous longstanding beefs with local Sureno gangs, DRGC's younger generation is now nearly half Latino (mainly Mexican) due to the high amount of Black families that have since moved away from the area since the 2000s. They also beef with WCNHC, ILP, MOB, DLGB, and A13.

Rancho Cucamonga

Section: San Gabriel Valley & Inland Empire

Also known as Rancho, Rancho Cucamonga is mostly upper-middle class suburban city in western San Bernardino County between Ontario and Fontana in the Inland Empire. Rancho is not known for much gang activity outside of occasional activity from CKS13, NAWGC and TCG; and is generally considered the most desirable and upscale town in San Bernardino County (maybe tied with Chino Hills) and better places to live in SoCal despite being nearby far more "banged out" and high crime cities like Pomona, Rialto, and San Bernardino.

E/S Pimp Player Hustler Gangster Crips

Section: San Gabriel Valley & Inland Empire

Formerly based out the Waterman Gardens Housing Projects, Large GC set on the east side of San Bernardino that's been around since at least the early 1990s. The term 4X originates from the fact that the gang was founded on the 400 block of Central Avenue before soon spreading into other part of the east side including the now notorious and demolished Waterman Gardens. PPHGC as a lone set holds one of the largest gang territories in SoCal/the entire state that stretches from the 210 Freeway down south towards the Santa Ana River. This is in part due to the fact that when the projects off Baseline and Waterman Avenue were shut down for demolition and renovation (now Arrowhead Grove) in 2013-2016, many of the residents were given housing vouchers to relocate to other parts of the city. And many families and PPHGC affiliates opted to relocate to various parts of the east side. PPHGC is closely allied with ABGC and beefs heavily with IEPJG, HTC, CGC, CCC, TMNHC, and all West Side and Neighborhood Crip gangs.

Rappers: Tinydown, KB, 4oeFace, A3zzzyk

E/S 1200 East Coast Blocc Crips

Section: San Gabriel Valley & Inland Empire

Main clique is Georgia Street Mob (GSM), 1200ECBC is the original, largest, and most reputable Black gang in Riverside County that dates back to the 1980s (then just 1200 Blocc Crips before turning ECC). Because they're an East Coast Crip gang, 1200ECBC falls under the BC/NHC/ECC card in prison, not the IE card like most other Black gangs in the Inland Empire, which lumps Crips, Bloods, and independent gangs together for the sake of protection against LA gangs. Historically 1200ECBC was engaged in a long-lasting gang war with ESR13, which led to many racially motivated homicides across the city leaving both civilians and gangs members dead as victims of gang violence. Though both gangs struck a truce several years ago. As a result, 1200 Blocc has been the target of numerous indictments and gang sweep operations by RPD. This is especially as 1200ECBC's territory directly overlaps and borders UCR as a campus, one of the state's larger public R1 universities. 1200ECBC main rivals are CBGC and PJC in Rubidoux. They also beef with SCMG, MAGC, BSMGC, DLSLB, and all other Blood and Hoover gangs.

Rappers: Reece 1200 (R.I.P)

South Side Gangster Crips (SSGC) Ⓜ️👌♿

Section: San Gabriel Valley & Inland Empire

Also known as Double S, the South Side Gangster Crips (SSG/SSGC) are an alliance/card of GC sets based in Riverside County (and some in San Bernadino County, though these ones don't claim SSGC, just GC/3X). All gangs under SSGC beef with 1200ECBC, WFBC, and all other Blocc Crip gangs. As most GC sets in Riverside are either influenced by or a branch-off of CBGC (except HSGC). The SSGC card directly beefs with the IEGC card (DBGC, HSGC, ABGC, YPGC, NAWGC, and MBC). As SSGC differs from IEGC in that SSGC gangs strictly run GC/3X when they hit the county jail and prison yards (CDCR), and not under the Inland Empire (IE) card, which traditionally encompasses all Black gangs (Bloods, Crips, or whoever else) in the Inland Empire. The IE card historically was formed for the purpose of Inland Empire gangs banding together collectively as a means of protecting themselves against much larger LA County based gangs inside county jails and prison. This was especially during the 1990s-2010s, when there was a higher presence of LA gang members residing, staking claim, drug dealing, and warring with IE gangs for territory before they became more relevant. This is especially where Riverside County is concerned, as prior to the 2000s the only known reputable hoods were PJC and 1200ECBC (with the latter running under NHBC in prison, not IE). This is partially what led to the formation of SSGC, as many members of CBGC, PAGC, and other Inland Empire based GC gangs didn't want to be forced to ally and program with their direct IE rivals while jailed/incarcerated, and instead chose to ally with traditional LA-based GC/3X powerhouses such as 83GC, AGC, BGC, and others. SSGC hoods also don't allow their members to claim anything other than GC/Treys unlike some mixed affiliation hybrid hoods under IEGC (i.e. DBGC claims both Criminal and GC due to ties with EMCG, while NAWGC despite being majority GC also has Bloods in their hood who simply claim NAW Gang). This has led to slight elitism amongst SSGC gangs in the Inland Empire. As SSGC members and their affiliates tend to view IEGC gangs as "watered down" when compared to their own politics. And their is an immense sense of pride in "movin' with the GC" and their own heritage, while pretty much rejecting any direct ties with other organizations (similar to the "No Kutts" movement with Bloods in the early 2010s). With SSGC affiliates usually harboring animosity towards BC and NHC gangs even far outside of the Inland Empire.

Part of East Side Business, SCMG is the largest gang in Moreno Valley with presence on the North and East sides of the city. SCMG was renamed again to Sex Cash Mafia Gang in the mid-2000s when they merged with North Side Villains (NSV) and Unknown Mafia Gang (UKMG). Thus why in their early years the gang was a mix of members that claimed Blood, Piru, Crip, and some neither which is unheard of when compared to traditional LA gang politics. Though these days the gang is none of the above and strictly runs SCMG and IE Card in jail/prison. As SCMG is somewhat notorious in the gang community for recruiting gang members that moved to Moreno Valley from other parts of the IE or LA. Main subsets are Hemlock Avenue (23000), Webster Avenue (24000), and Wolf Pack (WP). Their ongoing beef with EMCG, DBGC, and WFBC is responsible for a large amount of the gang violence that happens in MoVal. And as a result, SCMG is arguably the most hated gangs in MoVal and Riverside County, as theyve gained a reputation over the past three decades for shooting up parties and generally "marking out" members of newer MoVal/Riverside County based gangs. SCMG is allied with DLSLB and LGG under East Side Business/East Side Blood (ESB). Section: San Gabriel Valley & Inland Empire

Based in the Edgemont section of Moreno Valley, EMCG originally started as a branch-off of the Hoover Gang in SCLA. Edgemont as a neighborhood actually predates Moreno Valley, as this community was built during the 1960s before Moreno Valley officially became a city in 1984. The "U" area near Allies Place and Adrienne Avenue which is considered the heart of EMCG's turf had a notorious reputation of being "dope spot" for LA/IE drug dealers during the 1990s. As drug trafficking got so bad at one point that the city changed the street's original name from Republic Avenue to Adrienne Avenue. In recent years EMCG has also expanded their borders further west towards Day Street in what's traditionally EMLS13 area. Due to IE gang politics and their past alliance with Blocc Crips gangs (WFBC) they didn't start aligning themselves with HCG until recently despite claiming "Criminal Gang" in their name, and in the present day rep black rags. EMCG was formerly part of West 2 Da Town up until a incident between them and WFBC happened in 2022, and the two gangs are now rivals. EMCG is closely allied with DBGC YPCG, and FMGB. Main enemies are SCMG, SSMC, LGG, DLSLB, PAGC, CBGC, MBBC, and all other Blocc Crip gangs.

Perris

Section: San Gabriel Valley & Inland Empire

Small agriculture city in Riverside County, incorporated in 1911, Perris was originally a agriculture town partially founded by Hispanic migrant workers that emigrated to the area in the late 19th century before being named after locomotive engineer Fred T. Perris. Though the city would eventually modernize somewhat, Perris is still heavily considered a "desert farm town" when compared to more developed cities Moreno Valley and Riverside. Though despite this is still known for gang activity, as many GC, NHC, and Sureño gang members would set up shop here in the 1980s onwards due to the housing and rent prices being dirt cheap. It should be noted that Perris culturally is pretty much split into two or three cities itself, as the North Side closer to Moreno Valley where NAWGC is based is a heavily developed suburban community with houses that were pretty much all built in the last three decades. While the Downtown and western communities like Mead Valley and Good Hope are still heavily underdeveloped and mostly still used as "off the grid" farmland communities. The latter which can quicky be noticed by the lack of apartment complexes, gas stations, fast food restaurants, or even street lights on Route 74 towards Lake Elsinore.

Inland Empire Gangster Crips (IEGC) Ⓜ️⚫♿

Section: San Gabriel Valley & Inland Empire

IEGC is an alliance founded by NAW Gang (NAWGC) that most GC sets outside of Riverside fall under. This is as DBGC, NAWGC, MBC, all historically beef with SCMG, CBGC, WFBC, and 1200ECBC. As a result many Inland Empire GC sets and former independent black rag angs started falling under IEGC due to ties with NAWGC and the increasing emergence and rivalry with Blocc Crip gangs. Despite shared enemies, IEGC as an alliance is in direct opposition of SSGC gangs and their affiliates (CBGC, MAGC, PAGC, etc.) This is partially because DBGC was founded and influenced by members of 43GC, a historically reputable and founding LA-based gang that directly beefs with 83GC and AGC, who are more so tied in with CBGC. Therefore the SSGC vs. IEGC rivalry somewhat mirrors the SMG vs. Movin' Coast to Coast alliance in South Los Angeles. IEGC as a whole beefs with 1200ECBC, WFBC, MBBC, CBGC, MAGC, PAGC, SCMG, and all other Blocc Crip, Neighborhood Crip, and Hustler Crip gangs.

Banning

Section: San Gabriel Valley & Inland Empire

Small city/town in the San Gorgonio Pass region of Riverside County in the Inland Empire. Founded in 1913, the town of Banning was previously founded as a layover town for stage coaches along the Bradshaw Trail headed to-and-from Arizona during the gold rush of of the late 19th century; and the city was eventually named after stagecoach operator and local sheep herder Phineas Banning. Similar to other parts of the IE many Blood, Gangster Crip, and Sureño gang members would eventually set up shop in the area, as the city's insulation from the rest of the IE, affordable housing, and lower middle class population made it a hotbed for drug trafficking during the peak of the crack epidemic in the 1980s.

Hemet

Section: San Gabriel Valley & Inland Empire

Also known as Hemeth, the nickname "Hemeth" derives from the high population of methamphetamine addicts and other smokers that inhabit the town. Hemet is a large desert city located in the east of Riverside County/Inland Empire. In recent years Hemet has had a large migration of African-American/Hispanic residents moving here from larger SoCal cities like Riverside, LA, and SD. This is reflected in in the recent emergence of LA originated gangs like the Mafia Crips and WGC.

W/S Macc Boy Crips

Section: San Gabriel Valley & Inland Empire

Main clique is 25th Street (Fruitvale Avenue), are based out of the Hemet Vista Apartments. They also have a smaller cliques on 7th Street and 800 (Buena Vista Street). Mack Boyz was founded as a independent black rag clique/party crew in the late 2010s originally called Mack Boyz Money Gang (MBMG). Though as a result of the recent migration of many middle-lower class Black families from other parts of SoCal to Hemet, Mack Boyz have now become the largest Black/African-American gang in the city. Their main enemies are San Jacinto 1st Street (SJ1ST), a large Sureño gang that's been around for decades. Though due to the nature of IE culture the beef isn't necessarily racially motivated, as MBC/MBMG is allied with Minor Street Locos 13 (MSLS13), another Sureño gang also on 7th Street. And is known to recruit both local Latino and even White youths into their hood. Due to ties with NAW Gang in Perris most members now claim Crip/GC under the IEGC Card. They're also allied with EMCG and DBGC in Moreno Valley. MBZ mainly beef with WGC, PGC, CBGC, JBGC, SGMC, SCMG, HMT13, CLLS13, IELS13, and all other Blocc Crip gangs.

Rappers: Banditdamack, Buddha1k

N/S Toonerville Rifa 13 🇲🇽🇺🇸 (Glendale)

Section: Northeast, Southeast, & East Los Angeles

Founded during the 1930s, TVR13 is a highly reputable Sureño gang founded in the Atwater Village neighborhood of Northeast Los Angeles (NELA). Though over the years TVR13 has expanded eastward into the neighboring city of Glendale and northwards into Sunland-Tujunga. Toonerville 13 was originally known as the Latin Souls before renaming themselves based off inspiration from a train-oriented cartoon comic strip called "Toonerville Folks" and the formerly operational Pacific Coast Trolley that once ran thru their territory. TVR13 differs from most Mexican gangs in that they also heavily recruit both Caucasian and Armenian-American youths into their ranks. TVR13 mainly beef with TRS13, AVES13, WSLS13, FTR13, CXP13, and AP13.

Also known as Sereno Gang, main cliques are Locke Street and Ithaca Street Locos, are mainly based in the hillside community of El Sereno which is where they get their name from. ESR13 as held presence in this area (especially off Locke Street) for over half a century, and are somewhat seen as bullies of NELA as they outnumber and beef with most other gangs in their area (mainly BHR13, RH13, M13, and XV3. Though BHR13 outnumbers them due to being a projected-based hood). Though while still a large gang and highly active, ESR13 activity has dwindled somewhat in the past years due to gentrification of El Sereno and the surrounding NELA neighborhood (as WLA and SGV got more expensive, many Asian and White residents have since started moving in the area since the early 2000s, especially one from out-of-state that want to live in LA but don't want to move to SCLA due to it's even worse reputation for crime and gangs). Treys (3X) 3️⃣👌♿

Section: Central & West Los Angeles

The WLA Treys are a sub card of Gangster Crip sets (PBGC, GYGC, BYGC, BFGC, MFGC, and MGC) based in the West Los Angeles (WLA) region of the city stretching from Mid City to Santa Monica represented by the Texas Rangers logo. The WLA Treys have been around since 1975; when PBGC founder and then Hamilton High School student Jesse "Big Spider" James (top left Image) and his friends converted their break dancing crew into a gangs after numerous run-ins with local gangs from both WLA and SCLA. Though the WLAGC sets became more viral and known in media after the rise of PBGC/WLA rapper Big Sad 1900. Culturally, the WLA Treys gained most of their notoriety during the 1980s due to being some of the main beneficiaries of the crack epidemic in Los Angeles. As their direct proximity to more upper class/well-off districts like Beverly Hills, Beverlywood, and other WLA neighborhoods kept a wealthy consumer base to serve to (and rob on other occasions) to maximize profits in the set. Though the WLA gangs are also heavily involved in pimping culture, as their economic driven and hustler track record (both BYGC and MFGC were literally Hustler Crips (HC) at one point before flipping to GC) and ties with HCG and other GC sets in different counties and states has allowed to operate on different blades state/nationwide more freely than other gangs due to flexible politics outside of being anti-NHC/2X. At a certain point in the 1980s, the power held by the WLAGC axis caused the few kiwe rivals in the area and NHC-leaning hoods west of Crenshaw Boulevard to form the Deuces (2X) card (GGC, WBC, and VSLC) as a response to their rising power. The latter being a rivalry that still makes up most the gang violence that still does go on in the area even thru the 2010s/2020s (especially where SYC and VSLC are concerned). Politics wise, the WLA Trey gangs tend to lean the most pro-GC/anti-NHC of all Gangster Crip sets in SoCal, as PBGC, BYGC, and MGC are practically cliqued up with each other and the BPS gangs these days due to common rivalries with SYC, WBC, and VSLC most especially. And while not encouraged, more burnt out/younger members of WLAGC sets have even been seen on multiple occasions referring to other Crip gang members "crabs" both in-person and online. While the majority in the region, it should be noted that PBGC/BYGC/MGC and BFGC/MFGC have rivaled each other since at least the late 2000s. Though in the modern-day the beef between these sides has calmed down to to the point where most animosity between each other is kept at a social media or tag banging level, as all except MFGC) have more active and important rivalries with the same common enemies; SYC/VSLC. Though synonymous with WLAGC hoods, 3X is not exclusive to the WLA Treys, as SGV other hoods ABC (Altadena), DRGC, and ones ins Pomona are also claims Treys.

The Skid Row area of DTLA was once mainly controlled by 52BGC until many of their members were indicted and arrested by the FBI under a federal RICO Act in 2014. Section: South Los Angeles (West Side)

Also known as Dove Gang, main cliques are 25th, 27th, 29th, Second Avenue Gangsters (SAG), and Black Demon Soldiers (BDS) in Arlington Heights. Rollin 20's NHB via namesake is the oldest and original Blood gang that actually predates both the Bloods and Crips. As they were originally founded as a localized social club for Black youths in 1956 known as "Blood Alley" off Cordova and Normandie Avenue in the West Adams district before later officially consolidating into Bloods as an official organization along with APB, ESB, and BHWB in 1972. Though their twin gang the Rollin' 20's OLB also existed prior to this since the 1940s as simply the Outlaws before NHB convinced them to turn Bloods in 1972. RTB would soon eventually spread out to the Jefferson Park and Adams-Normandie districts. NHB have a an extensive history of beefing with the Harlem 30's and are cliqued up with the FTB and are allied with the BPS sets (especially CSB across Arlington Avenue. While still active and reputable, these days NHB is somewhat smaller compared to other historically major gangs in the city, as gentrification has made it harder to sustain recruitment. They share parts of their hood with MS13 and HPS13. Other feuds are with XV3, MCS13, ATC13, SYC, WBC, Rollin' 40's, 50's, 60's, 90's, 100's, and all other Neighborhood Crip, Blocc Crip, Avenue Crip, and most Gangster Crip (except WLA Treys) gangs.

Neighborhood Bloods (NHB) 🕊️🤙🩸

Section: South Los Angeles (West Side)

Also known as Dove Gang, NHB is a stand-alone sub card of the Bloods that represents Rollin' 20's NHB (R20NHB/RTB) in the West Adams district traditionally represented by the Nebraska Cornhuskers, Texas Rangers, Boston Red Sox, and later Tampa Bay Rays logos. NHB via namesake is technically the oldest Blood gang in the world. As they were originally founded around 1955/1956 as a social club for Black youths called Blood Alley off 20th/Cordova and Normandie Avenue during the 1950s. The name itself is rumored to originate both from term "blood" that was already heavily in use as a non gang-associated term by Black teens in this time; along with inspiration from the then popular Cold War movie Blood Alley (1955). Blood Alley by the late 1960s would begun to phase out, and by 1969 the next generation would eventually transition into the Neighborhood Bloods (NHB) in West Adams and Hoover Park Family Bloods (HPF) in University Park (a few decades before USC would eventually gentrify the area of NHB/HPS13 presence). Eventually the Neighborhood Bloods (NHB) across Normandie Avenue would soon start to become the dominant gang and eventually most of absorb HPFB and affixed the "Rollin 20's" part to their name by 1975, as many wanted to distinct themselves from IFGB and the Hoover gangs. NHB is also responsible for birthing other Blood/Piru gangs in other parts of Los Angeles County. As the Rollin 20's Outlaw Bloods (OLB) and both Neighborhood Piru (NHP) gangs in Inglewood and Compton are direct branch-offs of the original NHB hood in West Adams that still use the same hand sign.

W/S Rollin' 40's Avenue Crips 🇧🇿

Section: South Los Angeles (West Side)

Part of the Rollin' 40's and 4068 (RFC/OSE), also known as  A-Town. The Avenue side of the Rollin' 40's (RFC) is the westernmost side of their hood, stretching from Crenshaw Boulevard to Arlington Avenue. Located in the Leimert Park district, which is one of the few predominantly Black/Belizean American/African American neighborhoods left in Los Angeles County, and also the area where non-affiliate LA rapper Dom Kennedy grew up. Historically represented by the Los Angeles Angels and Arizona Wildcats logos, the Avenues clique is seen as the more preppy and "flyer" side of their hood (more expensive housing market prices, more Nike Tech fits, and fewer Pro Club t-shirt and wifebeater fits on members compared to what is seen the further east you go). Leimert Park itself also has a more positive and upscale reputation than the rest of South Central due to being the epicenter of Black Los Angeles culturally and hosting popular annual citywide events such as the Juneteenth Festival and MLK Day Parade, which are attended by thousands near 43rd/King and Crenshaw Boulevard. Their main beefs historically have been with BPS across Crenshaw Boulevard in a gang war that's gone on for over five decades and resulted in numerous incidents and deaths. It's also a rivalry that makes local social media news headlines annually when gang fights break out between youths from both sides (and their allies) on Crenshaw Boulevard during the annual MLK Day Parade. The Avenues clique also differs from the other sides (Western, Parcside, and Darcside) in that they historically push NHC the least out of all five sides, and instead primarily claim and fall under Avenue Crip (AC) along with RAC. They were formerly known as the Vernon Avenue Hustler Crips (VAHC) before turning Rollin' 40's sometime in the 1980s, but kept the AC identity. Most members (similar to 104HTHC being a Hustler Crip/NHC hybrid) claim either AC solely (mainly where the younger generation is concerned) or both. Though despite differences in lineage, both the Avenues (R40AC) and the other four sides (R40NHC) are mostly considered synonymous under RFC/OSE/Glove Gang. The Avenues clique's identity as a predominantly AC gang was further solidified after the war between former allies the Rollin' 40's and Rollin' 60's NHC broke out in 2013, as Rollin' 40's AC sits directly on the borderline at 48th and Crenshaw Boulevard. Due to the Rollin' 60's ties with the Rollin' 100's (600), the 40's have also had sporadic issues with the Rollin' 100's BC gangs. Darcside (R40NHC)

Section: South Los Angeles (West Side)

Also known as 800 Blocc or Coliseum Boys, the Darcside is both the area historically occupied by both Rollin' 40's NHC and STV43 and also the namesake of the easternmost clique of Rollin 40's NHC (RFC) based between Vermont and Figueroa Street. The origins of the Darcside itself is janky, as prior to the mid-1990s this area was originally claimed by the now defunct 43 Hoover Criminal Gang (43HCG). And this area used to be contested between 43HCG, We Don't Care Crips (WDCC), and Ancient Blocc Hustler Crips before the latter turned Rollin' 40's NHC and eventually took over the whole area. But via incarceration, murders (many which where committed by younger RFC members related to older 43HCG members) this area was eventually taken over by 40's. Objectively, DS has always been the most burnt out, fried, janky, and independent clique under RFC. Contributing to this notion is that this side of the 40's is more socioeconomic disadvantage (especially when compared to the Avenues clique in Leimert Park). As Vermont Square has a much larger concentration of working middle-lower class Black and Hispanic renter families in the neighborhood residing right next to the 110 Freeway. Where as the other end of their hood is predominately homeowners (can be seen as this section has far more closed businesses, cracked sidewalks, potholes, prostitutes (Figueroa Street), smokers, homelessness that makes it look far more "easty" in comparison). Political differences also stem from that most Darcside 40's members attend Manual Arts High School on Vermont Avenue as opposed to Crenshaw High School several lights west. DS were main side to beef to actively push the intra-NHC beef with the Rollin' 60's NHC when their war cracked circa 2013. The Darc in particular due to proximity mainly beefs with 51TGC, 52HGC, 52BGC, 53AGC, BPS, FHN, HOB13, and all other Blood and Gangster Crip sets (though all sides share the same enemies).

It should be noted that while still around, 52BGC is not as active as they once were historically, as the aforementioned federal indictments, incarceration, deaths, racial demographic changes, and many members simply moving on from the area has lessened the set's membership when compared other local Kiwe hoods or even their direct counterparts 112BGC. And unlike 52HGC or 53AGC, 52BGC is not known to recruit numerous Latino youths into the set for the sake of strength numbers. Their main beefs these days are actually DLGB, PBB, BSV, BSP, and more locally Varrio 50th Street (V50). Brims (FHN) 🎩🤘🔴

Section: South Los Angeles (West Side)

Also known as Brim Gang, the Brims are a subsidiary of the larger Damu (Bloods) alliance in the city and are represented under the maroon bandanna (Brims are maroon, Bloods are red, Black P. Stones are black, red, and green, and Pirus are burgundy). Founded around 1968, the Brims as a gang actually predates the Bloods as a criminal organization by a few years. As the Brims were originally founded by Eddie Watts Jr. (top left) and Kenneth Strafford as the Apple Hat Gang in 1968 before rebranding to Harvard Park Brims (HPB | Black Independent Revolutionary Mafia Soldiers) due to influence from the Black Panther Party a year later in 1969. Soon after, FTB and VNGB were soon founded as the three still active and existing branch of sets by Brim co-founders Eddie Trammell (FTB) and Dornese "King Swig" Young (VNGB). The Bloods were formed as a conjunction and direct response to the rapid rise of the Crips in 1972, with the Athens Park Boys (now APB), Bounty Hunters (now BHWB), Inglewood Family (now IFGB), Black P. Stones (BPS), and Piru Street Boys (now Pirus) banning together collectively under one identity. Though certain Brim factions such as the Dalton Gangster Brims (now Rollin 40's NHC area), Orchard Gangster Brims (now 52HGC area), 59 Brims (now 59HCG area) and more notably the Aliso Village Brims died out overtime. A long-extinct Brim hood called the Broadway Gangster Brims also use to control the area where 52BGC is now before the area flipped Gangster Crip and became the second controlled turf for BGC by the start of the 1980s, which is part of the reason the Brims still beef with BGC and the Hoovers gangs in the modern day. Their main three sets FTB, HPB, and VNGB have maintained a notorious presence on the West Side since their foundation. Ultimately leading to the remaining Brim gangs collectively referring to themselves as FHN (Fruit Harvard Ness), though it should be mentioned that this doesn't include the 59 Brims in San Diego, who are also their allies. Politically, the Brims differ from most other Blood gangs under the modern-day SMG alliance in that they have always been at odds with the Hoover gangs and to a lesser extent the Gangster Crip sets (especially where HPB is concerned). This had led to minor fractures in Damu unity has the younger generations of their other Blood allies such as BPS and IFGB often function with members from these cards in the present day due to their prioritization and shared hatred of NHC and BC gangs. Where as the Brims exist in "double-edged" paradigm where they are basically sworn enemies of the Hoovers (HCG) in the streets but are allied with them in the county jail due to broader SMG vs. 30s-100s gang politics. FHN collectively beefs with the Rollin' 30's  40's, 50's, 60's, 70's, 90's, 100's, ECC, SYC, WBC, 51TGC, 52BGC, and all other Neighborhood Crip gangs.

Section: South Los Angeles (West Side)

Also known as Hell Gang, 83GC is the largest Black gang in LA as far as territory goes, though the 60's and a few other gangs outnumber them in membership. 83GC was originally founded as Original Gangster Crips (OGC) before rebranding to 83GC afterwards. North Side, Farr West Side, Original West Side (retired due to disassociation with the letter "O"), Bacc West Side, and the South Side are the main cliques active within their turf. 83GC are mostly known for their beefs with the Rollin' 60's, 90's, and 100's that have been going on for over four decades. These beefs are what has led to the major split and animosity between most GC and NHC sets both across LA County and the rest of SoCal. This is due to 83GC being considered the founding Gangster Crip set and historically being the oldest, largest, and most influential and respected set under GC/3X. Making them the "flagship" Gangster Crip set that heavily influences GC politics nationwide. 83GC is seen as one of the more militant Crip gangs in the city, as their reputation for being extremely averse to newer gangs (both Crip and Sureño) attempting to set up shop near or within their boundaries has allowed them to maintain one of the largest gang territories in the county as mentioned prior; and is also known heavily for putting off their own members for not "programming" according to set standards or having undesirable allegations; something that's not seen as much in modern day LA gang culture due to gangs becoming more numbers driven. The latter also contributes to the beef and animosity between GC and NHC sets, as culturally both cards are seen a polar philosophical opposites of each other due to the differences within grander Kiwe politics, as while 83GC historically values community, militancy, and discipline; the Rollin 60's and other NHC allies citywide tend to be associated with clout, visibility, and boldness; and 83GC themselves have pretty much built their whole politics off of beefing and explicitly hating anything having to with NHC, BC, or their allies while also being one of the only Crip sets that's on good terms with IFGB and several other Damu gangs. As 83GC doesn't really beef with Bloods gangs and most of their allies outside of the GC card are Blood and Hoover gangs. DLGB and MFSB are exceptions due to 83GC's ties with 73GC, AGC, and BGC (especially where MFSB is concerned after the murder of 20-year-old 83GC member Alonzo "Tr3y Rich" Woodson in 2026, though encounters between the latter outside the county jail are uncommon due to geographic proximity). 83GC are currently still at war with the Rollin' 60's, 40's, 70's, 90's, 100's, 99MC, VSLC, SSLS13, and every other Blocc Crip and Neighborhood Crip gang.

Gang map · Gangs of Los Angeles (2026)

Gangster Crips (GC/3X) Ⓜ️3️⃣👌♿

Section: South Los Angeles (West Side)

Also known as Movin Gang, the Gangster Crips/Treys (GC/3X) are a card under the Crip umbrella traditionally represented by the Georgetown Hoyas (GC) and Texas Rangers (3X) logos. The GC card started as a result of the feud between Rollin' 60's NHC and 83GC that resulted in the GC card being founded at Saint Andrews Park in 1979, while 83GC itself had already existed as OGC in the area since 1973. Prior to this most Crip gangs in LA either fell under the West Side Crip alliance founded by Stanley "Tookie" Williams or the East Side Crip alliance founded by Raymond Washington. Most Crip gangs on the East Side would choose to align themselves with 83GC (except ECC and MSMC) under OG Melvin "Big Skull" Farmer (top left picture) who himself was originally from the east side; while most gangs on the West Side allied with the 60's under NHC/Rollin’ (except for the WLA Treys, Hoovers, and 99MC). This is due to the fact that the Gangster Crips have always had the reputation of being the more militant, violent, and grimy Crips, which more so appealed to heavily impoverished Black youths on the city's east side, as opposed to NHC gangs who are stereotypically viewed as the more “rich” and “flashy” Crips and therefore were typically most appealing to the slightly more “well-off” middle class Black youths on the west side. While almost synonymous, GC and 3X are technically two different things, as GC strictly refers to sets that claim Gangster Crip (i.e 83GC, 51TGC, AGC, BGC, etc.) and 3X/Treys are gangs that align with GC culture and politics but don’t claim it by name (i.e. ICG, PBC, SGC, etc.). Yet most gangs push both GC/3X. Since the 1980s, the Gangster Crips have been the main Crip card to expand into areas outside of just South Los Angeles. This led to them being one of the few Black gangs to have an established presence in areas with historically lower African-American populations like SFV, SGV, IE, Orange County, and Ventura County. As GC ethos often resonated with Black/Samoan youths from inland and suburban areas who were often outnumbered and at war with already established and often racist Mexican gangs. The GC card would eventually become the largest Crip card in California and the most dominant Crip faction outside of Los Angeles despite still being outnumbered by Neighborhood Crips in LA. Most GC sets practice the same agenda of "NK/OK/RollinK" regardless of their geographical proximity to the majority of NHC gangs. For this reason there is heavy animosity between most inner-city NHC and GC sets located far outside of Los Angeles. Though under the same umbrella, the GC card is one of the most historically divided in the county. As many major "GC vs. GC'' wars caused sets such as 4238GC, 87GC, 97GC, and BLGC to become allied with Rollin'/NHC/BC gangs due to their ongoing beefs with 83GC, AGC, and BGC, the three main gangs that dictate GC politics. GC sets that "clique up" with anything Rollin'/NHC/BC (i.e. Movin’ Coast 2 Coast and IE Card sets) are considered "watered down” by sets that abide by traditional GC/3X politics. GC sets that prioritize beefing with NHC/2X Crip gangs over older Blood rivalries often use the phrase “G before the C'' to signify their loyalty to the GC card alone as opposed to the larger Crip umbrella as a whole. In recent years the younger generation of members from GC sets have even gone as far as to associate with Blood, Black P. Stone, and Piru gangs due to their shared hatred of the NHC/BC/2X gangs. The banning together of certain Blood, Black P. Stone, Piru, Hoover, and GC sets have led to modern day alliances such as SMG that would not have been tolerated during the height of “Blood vs. Crip'' gang wars the city experienced in prior decades. Though 43GC is credited as starting the term "movin", 83GC is the oldest, largest, and most historically reputable. As without 83GC’s major influence across Los Angeles County and further, most GC sets wouldn't exist in the present day.

SMG/KMN (Suwoopin, Movin, and Groovin/Kill More Nkapps) is an unofficial alliance between various different Blood (Suwoopin), Gangster Crip (Movin), and Hoover Criminal (Groovin) gangs on the West Side of South Los Angeles. Though mainly a movement active in the county jail system, the SMG alliance has made it so HCG and their allies have established a near monopoly on pimping/prostitution market on Figueroa Street in recent years, as the Hoover gangs are notorious for extorting and murdering pimps from rival gangs that attempt to do business on the blade. As the increased presence of SMG-affiliated pimps has deterred many members of NHC, BC, and AC gangs from pimping on most of Figueroa Street since the formation of SMG early-2010s. Though the exception to this rule is between Gage and Florence Avenue, the stretch of Figueroa Street that 65MNHC now controls, as former SMG-adjacent hood PBHC has pretty much died out since the 2010s due to lack of recruitment in the area. Since SMG has low key become a culture itself, as it's become normal for SMG sets to respond to each other with “okilla” instead of “ok”, drop thumbs in music videos as a diss towards Rollin’ 30’s OHC, and “break the rollin” by doing it backwards (diss towards all Rollin’/NHC gangs) even by gangs from the East Side and Compton that are geographically further in the city from NHC gangs. Neighborhood Crips (NHC) ✌👍♿

Section: South Los Angeles (West Side)

Also known as N-Hood, the Neighborhood Crips (NHC) are a notorious and very large Crip card founded on the West Side of SCLA, are represented by the North Carolina Tarheels and New York Yankees logos. The origins of NHC date back to the original West Side Crips gang founded by Stanley "Tookie" Williams in 1969. When the Rollin 60's and 83GC started feuding in 1979, most gangs on the west side would align themselves with the Rollin 60's due to their perception of being the "flashy" or "rich rollin" Crips that were heavily focused on economic-driven crimes like robberies and home invasions as opposed to pure survival and gang-warfare like most hoods on the east side. Most gangs on the east side would later align themselves with their historical enemies 83GC under the Gangster Crip (GC) card. This was with the exception of the East Coast Crip (ECC) gangs who would all later turn Neighborhood Crip (NHC) or Blocc Crip (BC). ECC similar to the Rollin' 60's, 90's, and 100's were already beefing with the Hoover gangs and wanted to maintain their original East Side Crip identity while aligning themselves with West Side Gangs who shared the same politics as them. With the combination of most Rollin and East Coast Crip now falling under NHC, the card would become the largest Crip faction in the city. The reputation and clout of NHC was further propelled by the rise of LA rap legend and community leader Nipsey Hussle. Who was arguably the first popular gang-affiliated rapper to not only mention not only his gang but also the Crenshaw (Hyde Park) district, Rollin 60's, and NHC as a card in his music, thus and going by the "Neighborhood Nip" nickname. NHC politics most mirror those of traditional Crip politics, as the whole card has maintained beefs with the entirety of the Bloods, Brims, Black P. Stone, Gangster Crips, and Hoover cards for over four decades. The county jail dominance and vast membership of NHC gangs and their close allies in the city (mainly Rollin' 30's OHC, BC, and 120RAC) eventually led to modern alliances SMG/KMN/Thumbs Down. Were created as means of allying formerly neutral Blood, BPS, GC, and HCG gangs that all had pre-existing beefs with NHC/BC gangs.

Hoovers (HCG/HGC) ⭐🟠🆗

Section: South Los Angeles (West Side)

Also known as 716 Gang, HCG is arguably the most hated gang in the city, as they're known for having beef with both Blood, Crip, and Mexican gangs. The Hoovers have had presence on the west side of South Los Angeles since the early 1970s; and were founded by Alabama-born teen Joseph "Hoover Joe" Stanley (74HGC) (top left image) and his friends off 74th and Hoover Street as the Hoover Groovers. The Hoovers are known for being heavily involved in both drug trafficking and pimping/prostitution along Figueroa Street which runs through the heart of their hood. HCG was formerly part of the Gangster Crip/3X before splitting from GC during the 1980s due to early feuds with AGC, BGC, 43GC, 87GC, and 97GC (are now loosely allied with AGC and BGC in modern times). During this time HCG was also became prolific due to being heavily involved in drug trafficking during the CIA-funded crack epidemic amidst the 1980s. For this reason they still use the "movin" arm motion gang sign that GC/3X sets use. They would eventually adopt the color orange and start referring to themselves as Hoover Criminal Gang (only 52HGC remained GC). Though their main rivals by far have always been the NHC and BC cards, as their beef with the Rollin' 40's, 50's, 60's, 70's, 90's, and 100's especially is one of the deadliest in the city and dates back to the early 1970s. Other feuds with the FHN, DLGB, MSMC, ECC, and 120RAC have also accounted for many deaths on both sides. Their culture of beefing with almost every gang around them has led to them adopting the popular phrase "EBK" aka "Everybody Killer" due to the fact that they have so few allies (BPS, IFGB, 51TGC, 73GC, 83GC, GSWC, and a few other GC/3X sets being the only ones). HCG gained national media attention in 2020 due several of their teen members being arrested for the home invasion robbery and murder of NYC rapper Pop Smoke in the Hollywood Hills. This case brought further attention into the robbery and residential burglary (i.e. "flocking") culture that often targets wealthy celebrities and serves as a primary source of income for many younger members of LA/SoCal based street gangs. Despite being a predominately Black gang, a large portion of their younger members these days are actually Latino (usually Mexican or Guatemalan), with a few even being Asian and Caucasian. This is as HCG/HGC tends to be less picky and more inclusive when it comes to recruiting/putting on new members. Possibly due to the fact that many of their members are constantly either being incarcerated on long prison terms or dying due to the high amount of gang wars they've taken on over the years. As a whole, the Hoovers beef with all Avenue Crips, Blocc Crips, Neighborhood Crips, Mafia Crips (except 99MC), Brims, and some Blood gangs.

Blocc Crips (BC) 🩵♿

Section: South Los Angeles (West Side)

The Blocc Crips (BC) are a highly reputable but niche Crip card founded in 1971-1975 by the 107OBC, 113OBC, and UGBC sets (now known as Blue Flame Gang) within the Rollin’ 100’s in what’s now known as the Westmont district (also known as the 100’s) by Mississippi born teen William "Monkey Man" Johnson (UGBC) (top left image) and his friends off 105th and Normandie Avenue. Though east side gangs like 118ECBC have also claimed Blocc Crip since being founded. The BC card within gang culture is often seen as the more violent but still "flashy" counterpart of the Neighborhood Crips. Westmont has repeatedly had the highest murder rate in Los Angeles County and was consequently nicknamed “Death Alley” by the Los Angeles Times newspaper. Other areas claimed by BC gangs in nearby cities such as Del Amo of Carson (190ECBC) and the Eastside of Riverside (1200ECBC) also tend to rank near the top yearly in murder rates within their cities. Despite being smaller and often affiliated/confused with the NHC card, the BC card is actually its own separate entity. Though it’s rare, certain BC gangs do beef with NHC gangs mainly in the form of 111NHC/115NHC (aka OEF) vs. UGBC/107OBC/113OBC (aka BFG). And it's known in local gangland politics that Blue Flame Gang (BFG) in particular has documented bodies on multiple other NHC hoods in the city via minor incidents over the past several years, though most gangs abstain from fully beefing with them due to their reputation. Regardless, BC and NHC (NHBC) are considered almost synonymous and both function together and are usually housed with each other in the county jail system. The Blocc Crips earliest enemies historically were and still are the Hoover Gangs (especially where the Rollin' 100's are concerned), as the first documented murder between the two gangs was the shooting death of 107HCG youth Andre "Lil Ani" Jones by UGBC members in 1979. Decades later, the murder of reputable OBC/Rollin' 100s member Kenneth "KP" Peevey in 2015 led to the infamous #100Days100Nights shooting spree in South LA where civilians and gang members where either wounded or murdered over the course of one summer (most of the violence was the Rollin' 100's vs SMG); and later after the coordinated shooting and murder spree by 118ECBC of several Piru and SXL13 members in 2021. Though traditionally based in Westmont, other BC hoods have sprouted up in other parts of the county in recent years (mainly BDEBC (Hawthorne), 4CBC/57BC (Long Beach), and WFBC/MBBC/GBC in Moreno Valley. While other formerly neutral smaller Crip hoods CCBC and PNGBC have also turned Blocc Crip in recent years in Riverside; essentially making Riverside County a predominately BC-dominated area that only rivals the GC card influence and numbers wise in the region when compared to other Crip cards. 391ada085e866c13.h:
Gang map · Gangs of Los Angeles (2026)

Avenue Crips (AC) 🅰️♿

Section: South Los Angeles (West Side)

Also known as A Gang, the Avenue Crips (AC) are a low-key, reputable, niche, and smaller Crip card that's closely aligned with NHC/2X politics and uses the Arizona Wildcats and Los Angeles Angels logos alongside cerulean/teal rags. The Avenue Crips as a card were founded by RAC member Lavell "Screw" Player (top left picture) and his two younger brothers, Marcus "Spark" and Michael "Scragg" Player (R.I.P.), at Helen Keller Park around 1971. Avenue Crip was originally only pushed by RAC in West Athens and the Rollin' 40's AC in Leimert Park as a means of preserving the original "Avenue Cribs" identity founded by Raymond Washington in 1969 before the gang rebranded to the Crips in 1971. The Player brothers and RAC as a whole were close friends with Raymond Washington before he was murdered in 1979, which is why RAC and the ECC gangs are still closely allied today. AC was later adopted by the newer generation of GAC/GGC (Geer Gang) members off Geer Avenue in West Adams (though they mainly push 2X) due to close ties with the Rollin' 40's AC and, by extension, RAC. BAC (Mid City) and VAC (Gardena) are also newer AC hoods in Los Angeles County, though the latter two are unconfirmed to be stamped yet by the founding AC hoods. 120RAC has maintained a presence and notoriety on the West Side for over four decades, as deadly conflicts with APB, DLGB (especially), HGC, and SGC have made RAC infamous as a major factor in local gang wars in West Athens since the 1980s. Their two most prolific rivalries, with APB and DLGB, stem from the latter two gangs' refusal to turn Crip like most other gangs in the area during the early 1970s. Deadly wars with gangs like APB, DLGB, HCG, HGC, SGC, and PBC have continued since the 1980s due to close proximity and various incidents. Despite common misconceptions, the Rollin' 40's Avenues were the only clique of their hood that refused to push NHC at all until the late 2000s. Even then, many of their younger members have been on-and-off with pushing NHC due to the beef with the 60's NHC, differences in politics from the other RFC cliques, and the heightened distinctiveness of Crip card culture in recent years. RAC has also had on-and-off, sporadic beefs over the past few decades with Rollin' 60's, 100's, and LCG in Inglewood. The main difference in political ideology between the AC, BC, and NHC cards lies in the fact that both RAC and R40AC's biggest historical cross-border beefs have always been with Damu gangs throughout the decades, particularly RAC vs. APB/DLGB and R40AC vs. BPS/IFGB/VNGB. This is where much of the underlying AC vs. BC tension stems from, as despite their bigger reputation, BC gangs don't actively beef with all Blood gangs (such as DLGB) due to their focus on Hoover and GC rivals, whereas AC gangs are heavily anti-Blood while still beefing with Hoover and Gangster Crip sets. Several murders of RAC members by NHC gangs and vice versa, alongside various incidents with BC sets at Washington High School, are among the reasons RAC has never flipped to BC or NHC despite aligning with them under NBA/NHBC in county jail. Though these days, relations between RAC and OBC/UGBC are neutral due to shared rivalries with HCG. This trend of AC vs. BC tensions has also spread into the Inland Empire, as IAC (YFN) has been beefing with MBBC/WFBC since the death of a 16-year-old IAC member at Moreno Valley Mall in December 2025. Beefs with 87GC and 97GC would eventually crack off in the mid-2010s, while R40AC would eventually get dragged into beefs with DLGB and SGC through their ties with RAC (DLGB and the Rollin' 40's used to be allied under "Figarollin" until recent years).AC as a whole beefs with HGC, SGC, 83GC, 87GC, 97GC, IFGB, CMGB, DLGB, and APB, along with all other Blood, Black P. Stone, Hoover, Gangster Crip, Kitchen Crip, Mafia Crip (except 984MSMC), and sometimes Blocc Crip gangs.

Mafia Bloods (MGB) 〽️🩸

Section: Inglewood & South Bay

Also known as Crab Murder Gang, the Mafia Bloods (MB/MGB) are an Inglewood born Blood card founded sometime between 1976 and 1981 by CMGB off 104th and Crenshaw Boulevard in what's known locally as Bottomsville. Mafia Bloods (MB/MGB) as a card are historically represented by the Miami Redhawks, Minnesota Twins, and Cincinnati Reds (in the case of CMGB) logos. MGB has historically solely been pushed by CMGB as a namesake before eventually being adopted by several Inland Empire-based Blood sets such as BEBMB, SPMB, and GGMB in Rialto and Moreno Valley. CMGB themselves have gained major notoriety over the past several decades due to several deadly wars with nearby Crip gangs and later Sureño gangs (18th Street/XV3). As beefs with RAC, LCG, TCG, IVC, 104HTHC, and the rest of the Rollin' 100's have been well documented and helped publicize the "Inglewood Damu vs. West Side Crip" wars that have gone on since the 1980s. It should be noted that CMGB and IFGB/APG were not always allies thru time, as CMGB is alleged to have formulated after branching off from the original Chain Gang that eventually turned IFGB in the late 1970s. And beef between the two sets has flared up sporadically up until the last truce that's lasted since the early 2010s. Though historically a smaller gang when compared to their cousins IFGB, CMGB has had a significant mainstream media since the 1990s due to their appearances and references on Bangin' On Wax, Boyz N Da Hood, and Straight Outta Compton over the years that have essentially solidified them as a pillar set of Los Angeles/West Coast gang culture. In recent times, CMGB's main rivalries have shifted towards XV3, IVC, and the Rollin' 100's gangs, as their historical Crip rivals west of them (RAC, LCG, and TCG) while still active have mainly been weakened by heavy gentrification brought to Inglewood by the recent arrival of SoFi Stadium and the Intuit Dome several lights down Century Boulevard. As a result of said gentrification and heavily racial demographic changes in the area, CMGB has began heavily recruiting Latino youths over the past two decades (the only other Black gang/card that may recruit more Hispanics than them is the Hoovers or Swan Bloods). Up until recently, CMGB historically maintained close ties with DLGB/PDLB further down off Century in SCLA, though after the mistaken identity murder of CMGB veteran reputable Eddie "OG Stretch" Greene Jr. during a shooting spree targeting Crip gang members in Lancaster in June 2024 they no longer associate with each other. While spread out throughout three different counties, the Mafia Bloods as whole primarily beef with all Neighborhood Crip, Blocc Crip, Avenue Crip, and most Gangster Crip gangs.

W/S Hawthorne Piru Gang 🇹🇴

Section: Inglewood & South Bay

Also known as Hawthorne FAB, main clique is 135th, but they also claim 129th, 132nd, 134th, and 149th. Founded in 1982, HPG/HFAB is small but active Black/Tongan American gang based around 135th and Crenshaw/Doty/Kornblum Avenue. Their hybrid status stems from the fact that HPG is basically the older generation that claims Piru; while HFAB is the second generation and former clique turned Blood gang that shares the same blocks, enemies, and lineage. Due to HPG the city of Hawthorne ironically used to be a majority Damu/Sureño city up until the rise of local GC sets from the early 1990s-early 2000s. As HPG, 118GC, 118EMGC, HTFGC, and HLWS13 all fought each other (rivals 118GC, 118EMGC, MAGC, and HTFGC soon cliqued up as Inglethorne) over control over the Hawthorne/Prairie/El Segundo/Rosecrans corridor for several decades until HPG eventually phased out and most HLWS13 presence was pushed further west or south across Rosecrans Avenue towards Bodger Park. And only by the mid-2010s did HPG basically resurrect themselves in the form of HFAB. HFAB in particular gained notoriety locally after the 2026 chain robbery of BHWB rapper AOF Niino. These days they mostly beef with ABHC, VAC, MAGC, 118GC, 118EMGC, HTFGC, HLWS13, and most other Crip gangs.

W/S Stevenson Village Carson Crips 🇳🇬

Section: Inglewood & South Bay

Based in the Stevenson Village and Dominguez Hills Village Townhomes, SVCC is a somewhat reputable Crip gang based on the Northwest side of Carson that mainly beefs with 190ECBC and CVP. SVCC locally has a reputation as the "bougie crips" due to the fact that Dominguez Village is a gated community that's home to one of the most thriving upper-middle class Black communities in the county (though the same logic can be applied to 190ECBC as Del Amo is also a historic upper-middle class African-American community in Carson). SVCC also has a notable amount Nigerian-American youths due the high concentration of West African families that live over here. SVCC also beef with ECC and the rest of the Blocc Crip and Neighborhood Crip cards.

Notable Members: J Hood

W/S Victoria Park Carson Crips 🇳🇬

Section: Inglewood & South Bay

Main cliques are 181st and 189th, VPCC is a small and somewhat active Crip gang based around 189th and and Avalon Boulevard near Victoria Park as the name implies, and was originally founded as the Victoria Park Boys in the 1970s. Though a lot Black families do live here, the ones that do tend to be upper middle class West African (mostly Nigerian) ones, therefore the vast majority younger generation of youths that grow up here don't join gangs, especially in comparison to those in the Stevenson Village area (though SVCC has the reputation to attract more recruits in the same demographic, even teens that West African). Thus why Victoria Park is more so known for VPLS13 activity, a Sureño gang that claims the same area that they've had on-and-off beef with since around 2001, and also a hood VPCC allegedly got it's start from after Black members of VPS13 broke off and became their own hood in the 1970s. VPCC has only made a reemergence in the last decade during the late 2010s after being mostly inactive for years and it's become slightly more common more West African teen to join hoods (especially in Carson via SVCC, CVP, and other local Piru gangs). They mainly beef with 190ECBC, CVP, CPP, GAP, SDP, and most other Carson Piru gangs.

E/S 43 Gangster Crips

Section: South Los Angeles (East Side)

Part of the 4-Pacc (4238GC), are also known as Smak Gang. 43GC is the largest and most reputable of the three sets, as 43GC is said to be the oldest GC set and second oldest by name after 83GC, and have held presence on the east side around Gilbert Lindsay Park since 1971. Despite being the first GC set, 43GC and the rest of the 4-Pacc beef heavily with the Avalon GC sets (especially 40AGC and 53AGC), as 43GC actually used to be known as 43AGC for a short period before a fallout and war with 53AGC led them to drop Avalon from their name and form the Movin' Coast to Coast alliance with ECC in the late-1980s. This beef will still very active in the modern day, as hatred between the two sides and close proximity to each other (43GC is literally separated by one street on both sides from both 40AGC and 53AGC) has lead to the younger generation go 4238GC members to literally start referring to themselves as Avon Murder Gang (AMG) ("avon" is a local derogatory term used by rivals for AGC members). 4238GC has also had beef with the Broadway Gangster Crips (BGC) since 1979, which allegedly started after 52BGC members shot and killed 43GC member Amos “Gangster Lee” Thomas at Lindsay Park after a friendly football game gone wrong. Despite their early influence in forming the GC card, their close ties with Rollin' 30's OHC, Rollin' 90's NHC, ECC, and longstanding wars with AGC/BGC has led to the 4-Pacc falling out with 83GC and consequently most other GC/3X sets in the city over the years. Leading many GC members from other sets to suggest that the 4-Pacc should just drop Gangster Crip from their name as a whole and simply turn NHC, though this will likely never happen as tradition and history almost always trumps overs gang politics in regards to LA gang culture. 43GC also beefs with 51TGC, 52HGC, BGC, BSP, BSV, AFCB, MFSB, PBB, HOB13, and most other Blood, Piru, Hoover, Gangster Crip, and Kitchen Crip gangs.

East Coast Crips (ECC) 🈁♿

Section: South Los Angeles (East Side)

Also known as East Coast City or For Death Doe (FDD) gang, ECC is one of the largest Crip cards in LA, the ECC gangs are a direct derivative of the original East Side Crips gang started by Crip founder by Raymond Washington in 1969. As the area Washington grew up in, claimed, and was murdered in is now considered 66ECC turf. ECC is considered the east side counterpart of the Rollin' Crip card. Despite being one the bigger and most historically notorious cards in the city ECC is actually a subsidiary of BC/NHC, as every ECC hood either bangs/falls under Neighborhood Crips (NHC) or Blocc Crips (BC). ECC’s main rivals historically are MFSB, APB, AGC, BGC, HCG, and F13 prior to a truce with the latter in as part of an effort to defuse racial tensions on the East Side in the early 2020s. Their current beef with the Swan Bloods (MFSB) is considered one of the bloodiest gang wars in the city’s history, as the ECC vs. MFSB feud is responsible for many of the violent gang-related incidents and murders that have occurred on the East Side since the 1970s into the present day. ECC also began beefing heavily with GSWC in the early 2000s, which is part of the reason GSWC became more affiliated with SMG politics despite being Watts Crips. In more recent times ECC have now became primary enemies of the Compton Piru gangs (WSP, CPP, and FTP especially). As the formerly localized beef between 118ECBC/190ECBC and Piru gangs has now spread over the rest of both respective cards due to the Piru gangs being allied with ECC’s historical enemies APB/MGB.

Movin' Coast 2 Coast (Alliance) Ⓜ️🈁♿

Section: South Los Angeles (East Side)

Movin’ Coast 2 Coast is an historically important but now somewhat fading alliance between various Neighborhood Crip and Gangster Crip sets on the east side of South Central. Both the GC and NHC cards have historically always been arch enemies of each other since the war between Rollin’ 60s NHC and 83GC began in 1979. Though on the east side things were different, as many NHC/GC sets are (or were) cliqued up to go against common rivals such as MFSB, BSV, PBB, AGC, BGC, KC, and the Hoover gangs for the sake of "East Side Crip unity" that existed since the early 1970s when Crip founders such as Raymond Washington were around. This alliance has led to GC sets that fall under this card (mainly 42GC, 43GC, 48GC, 87GC, and 97GC) to have feuds with West Side GC sets (primarily 51TGC, 52HGC, 52BGC, and 83GC). As most west side GC sets actively beef with the entire NHC card (including ECC gangs) and have been doing so passionately for several decades, thus making many of the east side counterparts to enemies as well. What also makes MCC now somewhat irrelevant is that the younger generation of ECC members rarely even acknowledge this alliance to due being culturally aligned with west side NHC/BC/2X politics. And while neutral due to older ECC members upholding it, pretty much view 73GC, 87GC, and 97GC as 'non-factors" on the east side due to their quiet anti-GC stance and the arrogant, "high power" nature of most NHC members (i.e. "Ns don't need no friends" as an NHC slogan), creating a one-sided alliance. As a result, 73GC while small has pretty much exited this alliance regardless of common beefs with MFSB, as they are more so tied in with 83GC and the Avalon gangs. The most recent dagger in this alliance is that the ECC gangs have not only struck a peace treaty with 984MSMC, but have also became low key allied with them on local gang politics. E/S Mad Swan Bloods 🇯🇲🇧🇿🇲🇽

Section: South Los Angeles (East Side)

Part of VSOP, also known as Byrd Gang, this is the most notorious and active Blood gang on the East side. Their main cliques are 77th, 79th, 80th, and 84th, though some members also claim 89th and 92nd due to the fact that MSB and FSB are practically the same gang. The area west of Broadway has also recently been taken over by MSB, as their once small-time rivals 78HTHC have since faded out in recent years. MFSB is allied with the IFGB and CPFGB gangs in Inglewood as part of the Family Blood alliance. MFSB is known to beef with most other Blood and Crip gangs on the East Side. Their beef with ECC, 73GC, and 73HC are amongst the most violent gang feuds in the city's history dating back to the 1970s. Their beef with ECC in particular might truthfully be one of the worst gang feuds in American history, as both sides have been responsible for the constant retaliatory murders of each other's members since the 1970s into the present day. This is historically exemplified by the fact that MFSB embodies the stereotypical modus operandi of a grimy East Side gang in that they tend to prioritize killing their opposition over more economic ventures that West Side gangs pursue. This is why many encounters MFSB members have with their immediate rivals usually leads to gunplay as opposed to rival gangs on the west side that are more willingly to squabble their enemies in less "high stakes" situations. MFSB also feud with 83GC, 87KC, 88AGC, 984MSMC, 92BB, PBB, DLGB, HVWB, BWB, BMS13, and XV3. Though predominately a Black/African-American gang, their beef with BMS13 in particular has been furthered by MFSB's heavy recruitment of Mexican/Latino youths, which has somewhat drawn them into Mexican gang politics due to cultural ties and competition for new members in the area. Many of their younger members are either Belizean, Jamaican-American descent.

Mafia Crips (MC) 〽️♿

Section: South Los Angeles (East Side)

The Mafia Crips (MC) have been around the East Side near Main Street of SCLA since the 1970s and are traditionally represented by the Michigan Wolverines, Milwaukee Brewers, and Miami Marlins logos, and yellow bandannas (except for FTMC in Watts who wear brown). 84MSMC is said to be the original MC gang have formerly been a clique of their bitter rivals MSB (then just Main Street Swans) before turning Crips after several incidents between the two hoods; resulting in MSB turning Bloods while MSMC turned Mafia Crips. While 99MC on the West Side is a direct derivative of the now fractured 90 Hoover Gang that eventually split into 92HCG, 94HCG, and 99MC. Hence why 99MC is still loosely allied with the Hoovers to this day while 984MSMC have beefed with HCG extensively in an on-going deadly war since 2009. 984MSMC in particular was partially founded by both FBA and Jamaican immigrants who started immigrated to the to the Florence district on the East Side in the 1960s, many of which would end up joining or mentoring early founding MSMC youths. This where the drug dealing, scamming, and emphasis on "shotta" culture originates from within MC operations. 9884MSMC further rose to prominence in the 1980s due being one of the main factions to take advantage of the crack epidemic throughout South Central. Thus establishing themselves as one of the richer and flashier gangs in the city. It's even alleged in stories told by rivals that MSMC used to use a gold candy painted Cadillac DeVille with a sentry gun attached to the back to slide on ECC and MFSB members during the peak of the crack epidemic from the mid 1980s-early 1990s. The aforementioned ethos made MSMC even more appealing to many inner-city youths on the East Side who were typically more impoverished than their counterparts on the West Side of the 110 Freeway, as MSMC basically became known as the "money getting" gang on the East Side. Historically, MSMC has had major beefs with MFSB, ECC (now allies), 87GC, 97GC, and HCG most especially since the late 2000s. Mafia Crips also have established presence eastward in and outside the county in Pomona, Rialto, and Moreno Valley. Though considered a stand alone card under the Crip umbrella, these days MC politics more so align with NHC (except 99MC who are NK). As almost every set claiming Mafia Crip beefs with Bloods, Hoover, GC, and GSWC.
