Kitchen Crips (KC) 🔪♿

Section: South Los Angeles (East Side)

Also known as K Gang or Kitchen Gang, the Kitchen Crips (KC/KCG) are a small but reputable Crip card off the East Side traditionally represented by the Kansas City Royals and Kentucky Wildcats logos; as well as royal blue, sky blue, and white bandannas. The Kitchen Crips as a gang founded by Kenny "Smokey" Riley (top left image) and Keith "Kitchen Moe" Mosby after Riley his friends wanted to start their own gang off 87th and Central Avenue after allegedly regularly hanging around FSWC members on 103rd Street around 1973. Formerly known as the Shacc Boys, the Kitchen Crips are named after a now closed liquor store called Kitchen Liquor on 87th and Central Avenue by 87KC before spreading out to 116th and Avalon Boulevard (116KC). The Kitchen Crips are a small but notorious Crip card founded on the East Side of South Los Angeles (SCLA) that have been around since 1969/1970. Historically, 87KC/116KC main rivals have been the MFSB and ECC gangs, with a three-way "triangle beef"  resulting in numerous murders and other violent incidents between the three gangs along the Central Corridor and rest of the Florence district over the past five decades. Due to shared enemies the KC, AGC, and BGC sets were allied under a longtime alliance called "As, K's, and Ways", and most Kitchen Crip members run with the Gangster Crip/3X card in the county jail/prison system due to being small in numbers. Only recently have the KC and ECC gangs reached a truce, though minor incidents between still occur (especially between younger members). Though the RAC beef is still active, as despite the proximity between the two hoods KC vs. RAC has been -on-and-off as a beef since 1981 when the more notorious ECC war kicked off due to their ties with ECC gangs. Though even in the present day this beef is more of a chance encounter and social media beef between youth members, and both gangs have more mortal Blood rivals located just across the street from them (MFSB in the case of KCG). In past few decades the Kitchen Crips have spread out into other parts of the country (especially in Arizona, Oklahoma, Missouri, and Tennessee). KC in the present day beef with AMGB, DLGB, MSFB, VSOP, and most other Blood, Brim, Piru, Avenue Crip, Blocc Crip, and Neighborhood Crip gangs.

Bishop Bloods (BB) ♝🩸

Section: South Los Angeles (East Side)

Also known as the Bishops, the Bishop Bloods (BB) are historic sub card of Bloods gangs based on the East Side of SCLA founded by OG Bobby "Bishop Bob" Lavender (top left image) near 92nd and Bandera Street in what's now 92BB/ESB's hood. Bishop is historically represented by the Birmingham Barons and Boston Red Sox logos. ESB was founded as the original Bishop gang before the Bishop identity was spread over to PBB (then just known as the Pueblo Boys) from the Pueblo del Rio Housing Projects (Lavender allegedly had close ties in the projects and PBB at this time by the mid-1970s were already beefing with local ECC gangs) and BBWB via close ties between the three gangs eventually adopted the label as well via early close ties with ESB. Though similar to the Brims and Pirus, the Bishops actually predate the Bloods as an official organization by some years. The Bishops eventually transitioned from a local social club to an official Blood/Damu gang in 1972 alongside the Brims, Pirus, Athens Park Boys (APB), Bounty Hunters (BHWB) after the latter non-Crip organizations grew tired of the Crips terrorizing their neighborhoods and unifying to outnumber the latter gangs. For the past several decades, the Bishops have been mostly a legacy card held together by PBB, ESB, and BBWB as a trio, and while directly tied to beef with the ECC gangs, the Bishops have also heavily beefed with the Swan Blood gangs on-an-off for the past thirty plus years (especially where BBWB is concerned, as only Central Avenue separates them from FSB on the other side of 92nd Street. Despite their politics at face value, the younger generation at has some loose ties with AC and NHC hoods on the west side, as their immediate wars on the east side tend to be with SB and GC sets like MFSB, AGC, 4238GC, 87GC, 97GC, and the ECC gangs, with the latter having their own sporadic issues with other NHC hoods on the west side. As a whole, the BB card mainly beef with all Neighborhood Crip, Mafia Crip, Gangster Crip, and sometimes the Swan Blood gangs.

Hustler Crips (HC)💲🤙🟢

Section: South Los Angeles (East Side)

Also known as Hustler Nation, the Hustler Crips (HC) are a small and once much larger Crip/Independent card primarily based on the east side of South Los Angeles. Known for sporting green bandannas and the Hawaii Warriors logo, the Hustlers/Hustler Crips as a card were once way more prominent across the city. As many present-day Crip gangs claimed Hustler Crip due to the focus on drug trafficking and hustler culture that was dominant amongst Black gangs in during the crack epidemic of the 1980s when many sets were founded. Over time their influence would wane, and many gangs like BYGC, MFGC, and 71GC would later flip to Gangster Crip. Other sets like 46NHC and 104HTHC would eventually align themselves with NHC card due to influence from 111NHC despite still claiming Hustler Crip when the GC and NHC influence/ideology took over most of SCLA during the 1990s. Internal feuds between Hustler gangs sets like PBHC and HTHC also contributed to decreased influence and appeal amongst member gangs, and in the present-day 73HC, 88HTHC, 103HTHC, ESHC, and PBHC are the only existing original HC sets that still exclusively claim Hustler Crip. The Hustler identity has made a slight reemergence in the past three decades, as the inclusion of newer sets LBHC/MTHC in the Low Bottoms, 3BHC in Lancaster, and the emergence of numerous Hustler Crip gangs in the Inland Empire (primarily Rialto, but even then several of those have since flipped GC, BC, or even Bloods) has helped maintain their existence and further solidified their presence on the East Side and SoCal when the card has been borderline facing extinction years prior. As a whole, the Hustler Crips beefs are extremely flexible and are on a hood-by-hood case, as while most HC sets tend to lean more 3X/GC politically, the HTHC sets tend to ally with BC/NHC hoods. For this reason despite many HC hood being historically involved in gang wars many tend to view the Hustler Crips as a "get-along gang" as they're one of the few kiwe cards that doesn't have encompassing beef with any other particular card (outside of local Blood gangs), and many members will tell you this is purposefully as the gangs intend mission has always been "getting money" and hustling as the name implies. Their only historical and active card beefs are with the Mafia Bloods and Swan Bloods.

E/S Bounty Hunter Watts Bloods

Section: South Los Angeles (East Side)

Based in the Nickerson Gardens Housing Projects, also known as Relly City. BHWB is the largest Blood gang in Los Angeles membership wise, with cliques stretching from 108th to 115th (Lot Boys aka Shawlots), as well as smaller subsets like the Belhaven and Block Boys. BHWB origins predates the Bloods themselves, as the gang was formerly known as the Green Jackets in the 1950s-1960s that controlled three of the four housing projects in Watts (except Imperial Courts) before turning Bloods in 1972. BHWB are primarily known for having beef with Grape Street (GSWC) that's lasted for several decades, and contributed to the current longtime truce between BHWB and PJWC. Since 2010s, BHWB has had deadly on-and-off beef with CPP and WSP, as several incidents between BHWB and Piru youths stemming from incidents at Centennial High School in Compton led to BHWB starting a "PK" campaign and declaring war on all Piru gangs and aligning with NHC gangs like Rollin' 60's NHC and ECC. The latter moves were not viewed favorably by the larger Damu coalition (especially the Pirus and Black P. Stones); and BHWB members basically became regular victims of random targeted violence (chain snatchings, pack outs, shootings, etc.) by various Damu gangs countywide until all Blood, Black P Stone, and Piru gangs truck a collective truce by 2024-2026. Though the younger generation of most Damu gangs still barely associate with BHWB; especially on the West Side and Bompton, as BHWB are still opposite of modern-day SMG politics. They have other beefs with 984MSMC, FSWC, CPCC, MPCC, APB, MGB, MOB, FTP, HPG, HCG, F13, MTSW13, WVG13, WVL13, and sometimes the Black. P. Stone and Piru gangs.

Part of NWA, are also known as Westghanistan, main cliques are 134th and 142nd. WSP is the original Piru gang founded on Piru Street in Compton (aka Bompton), and one of the only three original Piru gangs actually on Piru Street (WSP, FTP, and 135P). WSP is arguably the largest, most envied, and hated Piru gangs in Los Angeles County amongst rival Crip gangs (especially ECC and Compton Crips) in the modern day. This is due to the fact that WSP is one of the only Piru gangs in Compton that hasn't waned in activeness or membership in the past two decades; as well as for being home and having produced most of the city's more well known rappers like Jay Worthy, Hitta J3, Wallie the Sensei, and most notably Kendrick Lamar who grew up on 137th and Parmalee Avenue. WSP is closely allied with Athens Park (APB) and Campanella Park (CPP) who are located a couple blocks down from them off Rosecrans Avenue. It should be noted that their 134th Street clique (Foe Line) crosses over Central Avenue towards Enterprise Park which is considered their turf too. Their main feuds are with CPCC, MPCC, TPCC, OSCC, FHCC, SHCC, NBCC, PBCC, SSCC, ECC, RAC, CVTF, CV155, B13, and most other Compton Crip, Avenue Crip, and Neighborhood Crip gangs.

Compton East-West Borderline

Section: Compton, Lynwood, & Paramount

The official borderline separating the West Side from the East Side of Compton that mostly follows the Metro A Line (formerly the Blue Line) train tracks on Willowbrook Avenue in the heart of the city. Though it gets tricky once you go north past Oris Street in FTP's hood because everything north of that is technically the unincorporated district of Willowbrook; which is considered by Los Angeles County to be part of South Los Angeles and not Compton. Therefore nearly every Black gang north of Oris Street outside of Front Hood (FHCC) and Anzac Gape (AGCC) claims East Side despite being west of the train tracks on Willowbrook Avenue. Though this also may have to do with the fact most of the Compton Crip hoods in that area (CPCC, MPCC, SHCC, and PHCC even though the latter no longer beefs with too many Piru gangs) have been beefing with West Side Piru (WSP) for half a century, with WSP being often considered the largest and most infamous gang on that side of town. So it's rumored many OGs from these sections also allegedly didn't want their hoods associate with the same geographic side as their mortal rivals and used the street names (i.e. East 126th Street on Central Avenue) as cop out to ignore geography despite them being located far from the hoods actually on the East Side of the Compton (i.e. MOB, LPP, LHP, SBCC, SSCC, WLCC, etc.).

Uptown Mafia Crips (UMC)

Section: Long Beach, Orange County, & San Diego County

Uptown Mafia Crips (UMC) is an alliance/sub card of Mafia Crip (MC) gangs in North Long Beach (BBC, BMC, and MMC) represented by the Memphis Grizzlies logo. As BMC and MMC both started after Mafia Crips started migrating to the North Side of Long Beach from Los Angeles in the late 1980s. BBC in the Carmelitos Projects would eventually adopt the MC card after the fact (reason viral rappers like Jooba Loc wear yellow bandannas in certain music videos). UMC like any other Long Beach Crip card only exists on a street level, as every Crip gang in LB runs Long Beach in the county jail and prisons. UMC as a whole beefs with ICG, GGC, NNGC, SMMHC, SBCC, SSCC, BBC (NS), and all Longo gangs.

Section: Long Beach, Orange County, & San Diego County

Part of Uptown Mafia (UMC), main clique is Andy Street. MMC are a somewhat small but locally reputable Mafia Crip gang that claim North Long Beach. Their beef with NNGC is especially well known as MMC and NNGC have fought over the Ramona Park are since the mid-1990s around when both gangs were founded; as MMC tried to force NNGC to become a clique under them, and NNGC would refuse and soon turn GC; resulting in a still active war between the two sides spanning three decades. MMC was eventually pushed further south across Harding Street; though they still claim a small sector of apartment complexes near 67th and Indiana Avenue. MMC is also closely allied and share most of the same enemies as BBC (NS) and BMC under the Uptown Mafia (UMC) alliance. They're also known for their back-and-forth beefs with ICG, SMMHC, and NSL13. Other beefs are with SSCC, ADCC, GTB, BNP13, ESP13, and NSL13.

E/S Insane Crips

Section: Long Beach, Orange County, & San Diego County

Also known as Baby Insane Gang or Sane Gang (BIG/ICG), main cliques are 21st, 23rd, and 5th Street. Founded around 23rd and Locust Avenue, ICG is the biggest and most storied Crip gang in Long Beach, and have a long history of beefing the Rollin' 20's LBC and Longo 13. In recent years ICG has used their increased membership and presence on the Eastside to take over over certain pockets of the city that were formerly claimed by other gangs (primarily RTC), contested, or traditionally had no gang presence such as 5th, 14th, 17th, and most notably MLK Park. They're part of the 3X/GC card and allied with the Hoover gangs in SCLA. They also beef with 4CBC, 57BC, BBC (NS), BBC (4X/NS), MMC, SMMHC, Rollin' 80's WCNHC, FHN, and all other Brim, Blocc Crip, and Neighborhood Crip gangs.

Rappers: Saviii 3rd, DW Flame, P Nice, Chief Rellz (I.I.P), Tayf3rd, KY3, Smakc, Utt Dawg, YNE Webb, Troop, Twiiinn, Mr. Bankroll, Yellxwtape

Locust Avenue

Section: Long Beach, Orange County, & San Diego County

Also known as Crip Street, 21st/23rd and Locust Avenue is the main historical cross streets and hotspot for ICG members; 23rd and Locust Avenue is said to allegedly be where the term "Crip Street" originates from after being coined by Long Beach and ICG rapper Saviii 3rd in the mid-2010s before the phrase was soon adopted as regular Kiwe vernacular by most other Crips county and nationwide (though many Compton Crips off Alondra Boulevard in Compton will debate this). 23rd/21st and Locust Avenue is still where most ICG members come from, though the gang has since spread out to other parts of the city formerly controlled by rivals; especially near 5th, 14th, 17th, and the MLK Park area.

E/S Rollin' 20's Long Beach Crips

Section: Long Beach, Orange County, & San Diego County

The second largest Black/Crip gang in Long Beach behind ICG, and home to legendary rapper Snoop Dogg and the Dogg Pound. Main cliques are 21st, 20th (aka Young Twenty Locs), 19th, 15th, and 10th Street. Rollin' 20's was started after ICG members living south of 21st Street of broke away and started their own hood in the 1980s. RTC are mostly known for their ongoing beef with both the Insane Crip Gang and Longo 13 that's lasted for many decades. It should be noted that the Rollin 20's LBC and ICG were not always arch rivals, as family ties between the two sides and a common enemy in ESL13 historically held the RTC versus ICG gang war to a sporadic level at it's worst. Though through the rapid emergence of ICG and their increased identity towards GC/3X politics due to LA politics spilling into Long Beach (and consequently RTC's alliance with Neighborhood Crip gangs) the younger generation of both gangs now considered each other hated enemies. They also beef with BP13, MMC, EBC, LBGC, NNGC, 19GC, and most other Gangster Crip gangs.

Rappers: Snoop Dogg, Nate Dogg, Daz Dillenger, King Twi, Trifling, 1sDaJp

Bandit Crips (BC/4X) 4️⃣⚫♿

Section: Long Beach, Orange County, & San Diego County

Stand alone Crip card founded by BBC on the East Side of Long Beach. Prior to them being enemies now, Many founding members of BBC in their early years (early 2010s) wanted to be 3X alongside ICG back when their main rivalries where with the Rollin' 20's LBC, Rollin' 80s WCNHC, and ESL13. Though due to early gatekeeping by ICG (who tend to act high-power and dismissive towards newer Long Beach Crip gangs, even ones that claim 3X/GC) and several early conflicts between the two, the Bandits opted to form their own card and began claiming 4X (partially named after 4th and Gaviota Avenue). ICG eventually would eventually become their worst enemies along with BBC (Bricc Boys) from the North Side. And the beef with 20s was eventually truced. Since the area east of Alamitos Avenue historically had no other major Black/Crip gangs (only ABZ, SOSGC, and ESL13 held presence, with the latter being notoriously racist towards even non-affiliate Blacks and Asians). The recruitment vacuum eventually led to BBC becoming the fourth largest Crip gang in the city only behind 20's, 80's, and ICG. Should be noted that this was also possible is because most Long Beach Crip gangs run under the LBC (Long Beach Crip) card in the county, and not under LA-based cards like GC, NHC, etc.). Therefore past street-level politics most of these gangs operate as one in the county jail and prison yards regardless (except for newer BBC rivals 57BC, who run under NHBC). The only other kiwe gang that runs under 4X on a street-level is PPHGC in San Bernardino. Who due to being GC and located in the Inland Empire are irrelevant and far removed from Los Angeles County and Long Beach gang politics.

W/S Santa Nita Rifa 13 🇲🇽

Section: Long Beach, Orange County, & San Diego County

Santa Nita Rifa (SNR13) is one of the oldest, largest, and most active gangs in Santa Ana. SNR first started out as a car club called the Midnight Cruisers during the 1950s in Barrio Santa Anita before evolving into a street gang later during the 1970s. SNR is well-known in Orange County because of the amount of gang related crimes being committed throughout SNR's territory, and because of the infamous Harbor Blvd, which was known for the pimps and prostitution problems that plagued the neighborhoods for decades.

Because of the high crime rate in this location, Santa Ana placed SNR under a gang injunction in 2006 to curtail the crimes in this area. SNR mainly operates in the area between Westminster Blvd, Harbor Boulevard McFadden Ave, and The Santa Ana Riverbed. SNR13 beefs heavily with MSR13.

W/S F Troop Rifa 13 🇲🇽

Section: Long Beach, Orange County, & San Diego County

F Troop (FTR13) is one of Santa Ana's largest gangs, main cliques are Barrio Artesia, Salvador Park, and Western Avenue. The origin of FTR name is still unclear, but many people have said that the gang's name derived from the TV show called F-Troop, which aired in 1965, however, some people denies this claim. Furthermore, FTR is also one of the oldest gangs in Santa Ana, which was formed sometime during the mid 1960s in Orange City before establishing itself in Barrio Artesia, Santa Ana. Some people claim that FxTroop originated in Santa Ana though.

In the 1970s and 1980s, FxTroop was the largest gang in all of OC which had about 8 to 10 cliques. During the 1980s and 1990s several FxTroop cliques separated and became independent gangs. Several gangs such as 7th Street, Barrio South Side, Brook Street, Highland Street, East Side, Walnut Street, and more were once a part of FxTroop before separating.

E/S Tiny Rascal Gang (Santa Ana)

Section: Long Beach, Orange County, & San Diego County

Minnie Street clique, Tiny Rascal Gang (TRG) is an Asian gang that formed in Long Beach in the mid 1980s by Cambodian refugees to protect themselves against the East Side Longos (ESLx3) gang who harassed and bullied them during the 1980s. In the early 1990s, TRG allowed all ethnicity to join its gang and quickly became the largest Asian street gang in the US, with an estimated 5,000 members across the USA. TRG second oldest clique is in Santa Ana, after the East Side Long Beach clique. Minnie St TRG established itself during the mid 1980s around the Bishop Manor and the Minnie St apartments where hundreds of Cambodian and Vietnamese families lived during that time. Nowadays, TRG's presence on Minnie St is not as prevalent as the past since many Asian families moved out, but there're still members living there. TRG is mostly nomadic now and its members are spread throughout Santa Ana, Tustin, Westminster, and Garden Grove.

55 Freeway/Newport Boulevard

Section: Long Beach, Orange County, & San Diego County

The informal divider between North Orange County and South Orange County, the 55 Freeway historically represents the dividing line between Orange County's predominately Asian and Hispanic cities like Anaheim, Garden Grove, and Santa Ana while anything south of here tends to be more upper class and historically White exclusive enclave coastal cities like Newport beach, Irvine (mostly Asian now but still affluent), Lake Forest, San Clemente, and San Juan Capistrano. As even the Black, Asian, Polynesian, and Hispanic families that could afford it at the time were legally banned and redlined from purchasing housing south of here (and most of OC except for Anaheim and Santa Ana) until the Fair Housing Act of 1968. This can be seen in he extreme lack of Hispanic gang territories south/east of the freeway outside of Family Mob 13 (FM13), Varrio Chicos San Clemente (VCSC13), and San Juan Capistrano 13 (SJC13). As the majority of youths who are privileged enough to grow up in the latter cities are too well resourced to generally want to partake in any type of gang activity.
